title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a case of a synthetic image presented as a factual record of real people. The alteration happened at the point of publication, in promotional material for campus banners, where an edited photograph was treated as an ordinary photograph of a Stanford event. The failure mode is not a model asserting something false in text but a generated or edited image standing in for documentary evidence, with no disclosure that it had been changed.

The university's own policy already prohibited using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, facilities, or achievements, and the university said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Catching it would have required a review step comparing the material against the original image before it went up, and a disclosure that AI had been used. Both were available inside the institution, and neither was applied.

What is not established is who performed the alteration, why it was made, or what consequences followed. The university acknowledged the change and the policy violation, and the reporting does not establish intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
A Stanford University photo from a 2024 Lunar New Year party originally showed Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students. The dining service posted it online the next day. When Stanford used the image on campus banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said it was upsetting.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy bans using A.I. to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
